rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for toasted bread or a piece of toast.

example.english: I usually have toast for breakfast.
example.traditional: 我朝早通常食多士做早餐。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ziu1 zou2 tung1 soeng4 sik6 do1 si2 zou6 zou2 caan1

rows.note: Use this for a formal drinking salute or toast at a reception or ceremony.

example.english: At the ceremony, the master of ceremonies proposed a toast.
example.traditional: 典禮上，主禮人提議祝酒。
example.jyutping: din2 lai5 soeng6 zyu2 lai5 jan4 tai4 ji5 zuk1 zau2

rows.note: Use this for a person who is especially celebrated or favored in a social circle.

example.english: At tonight’s birthday banquet, they were the toast of the evening.
example.traditional: 今晚壽宴，佢係全場嘅紅人。
example.jyutping: gam1 maan5 sau6 jin3 keoi5 hai6 cyun4 coeng4 ge3 hung4 jan4

rows.note: Use this when the doomed person or group is being treated as expendable or sacrificed.

example.english: These recruits were sent to the front line; they were basically toast.
example.traditional: 呢班新兵俾人派去前線，根本就係炮灰。
example.jyutping: ni1 baan1 san1 bing1 bei2 jan4 paai3 heoi3 cin4 sin3 gan1 bun2 zau6 hai6 paau3 fui1
